title: Author a component and reuse it, start to finish
goal: The whole point of this line of work, tried as one sitting: draw a control, turn it into a component, drop three copies, make its label adjustable, change one copy, then edit the original and watch them all follow. And prove that taking a screenshot, measuring it and redlining it is exactly as it was.
notes:
Step E9 of docs/design/ui-building.md, the acceptance bar for the whole epic; the user named this scenario on 2026-09-02. Use Scripts/playtest.sh with a new walk under Scripts/playtest/. This task is claimed only after the instance, override and built-in library tasks are done; set its deps to them when they exist.

Objective: ui-components (staged now, under the focus). The acceptance bar for the whole sub epic, and the proof that none of it disturbed capture and redline.
acceptance: A scripted walk drives the whole scenario on the probe app and every step is captured as a picture
The audit reads as a sitting a person can repeat in under five minutes, with the pictures in order
A second walk captures a screenshot, measures it and copies a spec list, and the audit states that nothing about that flow changed
Every rough edge found is filed as a follow-up task, named in the audit
Anything that cannot be done at all is stated plainly rather than worked around

log.note: adversarial review before building: this is an audit step, not a feature. Shortest version that delivers the value = one walk for the scenario plus the walk that ALREADY existed for redline, since a pre-existing walk still passing is a stronger 'nothing changed' than a new one written to pass. Added one new short walk on top (component dropped onto a capture, then measured) because 'does redlining break when the document holds a component' was the only question neither walk answered.
component-end-to-end-walk.json green first run, 70 steps, 19.4s, real -sc.png captures (Screen Recording granted). Pill reads 'Updated · 3 copies of Save button'; one undo reverts all four.
redline-walk.json (predates this epic) re-run unchanged: green, 70 steps, same five measurements and same spec list text.
redline-with-components-walk.json green: measurements identical either side of dropping a component, component absent from the spec list.

harness gap found and fixed: playtest dropComponent only knew about a component already in the document, so a walk could not drag a STARTER tile onto the canvas, which is the first thing a person does. Falls back to selectedStarterComponent now; the real path (placeComponent) always handled both.

cannot be done at all, stated rather than worked around: a whole-screen capture cannot be scripted (the overlay owns every display and the pointer). Ran the standalone --capture-diag; it reported the screen LOCKED, which invalidates its own readings. Recorded in the audit's rough.
Scripts/test.sh green: 1852 tests, 189 suites. Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-03-component-end-to-end.json with six real captures.

Two scripted walks and an audit. component-end-to-end-walk.json drives draw, group, make component, expose wording, three copies, override one, edit the original (pill: Updated, 3 copies of Save button; one undo reverts all four), green in 19s with real screen captures. redline-with-components-walk.json plus the pre-existing redline-walk.json prove measure and spec export are unchanged, with and without a component in the document.
